Explanation: The Luxury Listing is the Core Value Unit: a specific luxury item from a brand or boutique, represented with product, price, size and availability information so it can be discovered and purchased globally through Farfetch.
Farfetch operates the luxury marketplace and customer interface. Coupang acquired the Farfetch business and assets in January 2024.
Farfetch turns fragmented global luxury inventory into one searchable and transactional destination.
Aggregated demand and supply can increase marketplace liquidity and generate transaction-related economics.
Farfetch must coordinate premium service, partner economics, global fulfillment and profitability across a fragmented supply base.
Farfetch coordinates discovery, ordering, customer payment and commercial settlement with the selling partner.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Order / Pay — Customers place orders and payment through Farfetch's unified checkout. | → Consumer · Discovery / Service — Farfetch provides global discovery, checkout, customer support, shipping coordination and returns. | ← Provider · Listing / Stock — Brands and boutiques provide product listings, inventory availability and commercial data. | → Provider · Demand / Payout — Farfetch routes customer demand to the selling partner and remits the relevant proceeds after the transaction. | → Partner · Volume / Labels — Farfetch orchestrates shipping options and creates parcel volume across its distributed retail network. | ← Partner · Tracking / Delivery — Carrier status and delivery events feed Farfetch's customer-service, tracking and return processes.

Explanation: Farfetch governs retail-partner eligibility, listing quality, customer service, returns and marketplace standards.
Farfetch attracts luxury demand through campaigns, search, editorial merchandising, exclusives and brand storytelling.
Farfetch operates discovery, checkout, partner integration, customer support, settlement and shipping orchestration.
Its global retail network, customer base, fashion data and marketplace technology are strategic resources.
Luxury Customers use Farfetch to discover and buy products from brands and boutiques around the world through one interface.
Customers want to find desirable luxury products, including pieces that may not be available in their local market.
Farfetch combines fragmented global inventory into a broad selection with one discovery and checkout experience.
Luxury e-commerce creates friction around price, fit, customs, returns, delivery time and cross-border complexity.
Customers place orders and pay through Farfetch even when the underlying sale is with a third-party partner boutique.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Order / Pay — Customers place orders and payment through Farfetch's unified checkout. | ← Owner · Discovery / Service — Farfetch provides global discovery, checkout, customer support, shipping coordination and returns. | → Provider · Purchase / Demand — The underlying purchase contract is with the partner boutique or brand, so the customer's order creates direct demand for that Provider's product. | ← Provider · Luxury Item — The selling partner supplies the purchased item, which is shipped from that partner's inventory to the customer. | ← Partner · Delivery — The logistics carrier physically delivers the purchased product to the customer.

Logistics Carriers are the most business-model-critical external complement in the global marketplace boundary. Farfetch currently ships worldwide primarily through DHL, with UPS and other carriers used in selected markets, so distributed boutique inventory can reach customers without Farfetch owning the stock.
Carriers must move high-value products reliably across the local and international routes connecting Farfetch partners with customers.
Farfetch creates recurring premium parcel volume across many countries and retail origins.
Cross-border luxury shipments face customs, security, delivery-time and loss or damage risk.
Providers hand parcels to the carrier network; carriers move them to customers and support the reverse flow for returns.
